# NVDA — Quantitative Fundamental Attractiveness Report

**Decision date: 2026-06-05 | Filing anchor: Q1 FY2026 (period end 2026-04-26, filed 2026-05-20)**

---

## 1. Revenue, Earnings, and Margin Trajectory

NVDA's most recent quarter (Q1 FY2026, 2026-04-26) delivered revenue of $81.61B and EPS diluted of $2.39. YoY revenue grew +85.2% from $44.06B (Q1 FY2025) and EPS grew +214.5% from $0.76. QoQ, revenue rose +43.2% from $57.01B (Q3 FY2025) and EPS +83.8% from $1.30. This is a parabolic earnings trajectory — net income of $58.32B in a single quarter, up +210.6% YoY from $18.77B.

Margins are expanding at every level:
- **Gross margin**: 74.9% ($61.16B / $81.61B), up from 60.5% in Q1 FY2025 and 73.4% in Q3 FY2025.
- **Operating margin**: 65.6% ($53.54B / $81.61B), up from 49.1% a year ago and 63.2% last quarter.
- **Net margin**: 71.5% ($58.32B / $81.61B), up from 56.0% in Q3 FY2025. Notably, net income ($58.32B) exceeds operating income ($53.54B), indicating significant non-operating income likely from the growing investment portfolio (total assets doubled to $259.47B).

The margin story is one of operating leverage at scale — cost of revenue of $20.46B on $81.61B sales, with operating expenses absorbing only 9.3% of revenue above COGS.

## 2. Cash Generation and Balance-Sheet Resilience

**Cash flow** is robust. Operating cash flow in Q1 FY2026 was $50.34B, up +112.0% QoQ from $23.75B (Q3 FY2025) and +83.6% YoY from $27.41B. OCF-to-net-income conversion stands at 86.3% ($50.34B / $58.32B) — strong, though not exceeding 100%, so no obvious accrual red flags. Free cash flow data is unavailable, but operating cash flow alone is substantial.

**Balance sheet** is fortress-grade. Total equity has grown from $83.84B to $195.47B in four quarters (+133%), while total debt is essentially flat at $8.47B. The debt-to-equity ratio stands at 4.3%. Total liabilities of $64.00B are modest relative to $259.47B in assets. The company is internally funding its growth entirely; leverage is immaterial. The near-tripling of total assets (from $125.25B to $259.47B) in a year also signals aggressive reinvestment, likely in working capital and financial assets to support the ramp.

## 3. Valuation versus Own History

The stock trades at **PE diluted = 33.4x** (2026-06-04), which sits at the **floor** of its 365-day range of 32.3x–66.8x. This PE was established after Q1 FY2026 earnings were incorporated (filing 2026-05-20). On 2026-05-01, before the Q1 print, PE was 56.2x — the market has absorbed a ~40% PE compression in one month as earnings surged into the denominator.

**Price-to-book** of 27.3x is similarly at the bottom of its 26.3x–57.8x range. The sparse history shows PB declining from 41.1x (Jun 2025) to 27.3x, while ROE has remained extraordinarily high at 81.7% (latest) vs. 91.6% a year ago. The PB contraction on stable-to-high ROE signals the market is not chasing the earnings expansion — it is pricing durability concerns.

The implied **earnings yield** of 3.0% against a 10-year Treasury yield of 4.47% creates a negative equity risk premium on the headline PE, which is the key macro-tension point. However, the company's earnings growth rate (EPS +214.5% YoY) generates an implied PEG near 0.15x — extremely low if growth persists even at a fraction of this pace.

## 4. Price Context versus Fundamental Path

Price closed at $218.66 on 2026-06-04, within a 52-week range of $138.83–$236.54 (89th percentile). The quarterly price trajectory shows acceleration: +6.4% (Sep–Dec 2025), +1.0% (Dec 2025–Mar 2026), then **+19.3%** (Mar–Jun 2026) to $218.66 from $183.34. The recent rally coincides with the Q1 FY2026 earnings catalyst (filed 2026-05-20). The stock remains ~7.5% below its all-time high of $236.54 despite delivering the strongest quarterly earnings in its history. Price has not fully caught up to the earnings inflection.

## 5. Macro and Sentiment Overlays

**Macro** is mixed. The 10-year Treasury yield has risen to 4.47% (from 4.12%, +8.5% over 90 days), which mechanically compresses duration-sensitive valuations. The 2-year yield rose to 4.05% (+13.8%), flattening the curve (10Y-2Y spread: 0.42%, down from 0.56%). The VIX has collapsed from 25.5 to 15.4 (−39.6%), signaling broadly risk-on conditions. Oil is elevated at $96.83. The Fed funds rate at 3.63% is stable-to-easing. Net assessment: rising long rates are a headwind for the multiple, but collapsing vol and easing policy rate partially offset. This does not override the fundamental picture but explains some of the PE compression.

**News sentiment** (90-day mean: 0.459) is moderately positive. The most recent days show elevated readings: 0.875 (2026-06-01), 0.778 (2026-06-02), settling at 0.522 (2026-06-04). There was a negative outlier of −0.143 on 2026-05-15. Overall, sentiment is constructive but not euphoric — no extreme readings that would signal contrarian risk.

## 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside and Downside

**Upside:**
- PE of 33.4x is at the bottom of its historical range while delivering the strongest earnings quarter on record. If even a fraction of the growth trajectory persists, the earnings yield compresses toward Treasury yields, and the multiple has room to re-rate back toward the mid-range (45–55x).
- Operating cash flow of $50.34B in a single quarter provides enormous capital return and reinvestment optionality.

**Downside:**
- Growth durability is the core risk. A single quarter's +85% revenue growth and +214% EPS growth are inherently difficult to sustain. Any deceleration — even to still-strong levels — could cause the PE to compress further if the market is already pricing normalization at 33x.
- The negative equity risk premium (3.0% earnings yield vs. 4.47% 10Y) means the stock is expensive on an absolute basis if growth stalls. In a higher-rate regime, even "cheap for NVDA" may not be cheap in absolute terms.
- Total assets doubling in a year (to $259.47B) warrants monitoring for asset quality — the composition is unspecified, but rapid balance-sheet expansion can embed latent risks.

## 7. Provisional Conclusion

**Quantitatively attractive.** NVDA's business trajectory is among the strongest in the dataset: revenue nearly doubled YoY, EPS tripled, margins are expanding across every metric, cash generation is enormous ($50.34B OCF in one quarter), and the balance sheet is pristine (4.3% debt-to-equity). The stock sits at the low end of its own valuation history (PE 33.4x vs. 32.3–66.8x range, PB 27.3x vs. 26.3–57.8x range) despite delivering its best fundamental quarter. The market's PE compression reflects legitimate durability concerns and rising rates, but on the numbers alone — earnings trajectory, margin expansion, cash conversion, and balance-sheet strength — the fundamental case is compelling at current multiples relative to the company's own history. The risk is that growth deceleration proves sharper than the multiple discount already implies.

---

# NVDA — Qualitative Franchise Assessment

**Decision date:** 2026-06-05 | **Instrument:** NVDA

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

Nvidia operates a fabless semiconductor model designing GPUs, CPUs, networking fabrics, and software for AI infrastructure. The Data Center segment generated $75.2B in Q1 FY2027 (+92% YoY), representing ~92% of total revenue ($81.6B, +85% YoY). Within Data Center, networking revenue surged 199% YoY to $14.8B, signaling Nvidia is selling full-stack architecture — chips, interconnects, and software — not standalone silicon. The company introduced new segment reporting in Q1 FY2027 splitting Data Center into Hyperscale ($37.9B, +115% YoY) and AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise ($37.4B, +74% YoY), deliberately reframing the narrative away from hyperscaler dependency.

**Competitive moat** rests on three reinforcing pillars: (1) the CUDA software ecosystem with 5M+ developers, creating deep switching costs; (2) full-stack vertical integration spanning GPUs, CPUs (new Vera), NVLink interconnects, InfiniBand/Spectrum-X networking, and enterprise software; and (3) a fabless model that converts revenue to cash at extraordinary rates — $48.6B free cash flow in Q1 alone, $106B trailing twelve months, against capex of just $1.8B. Industry estimates place Nvidia at ~86% of the AI GPU market (companieshistory.com) and 81% of the data center chip market by revenue (IDC, per ainvest.com).

**Structural growth vectors** extend well beyond the current GPU franchise. The Vera CPU, now in full production, opens a $200B total addressable CPU market with $20B in standalone CPU revenue projected this fiscal year. The Vera Rubin platform is ramping into full production for fall 2026 shipments, with 150+ Taiwan-based partners and 350+ factories across 30 countries. Physical AI (autonomous vehicles, robotics, industrial digital twins) generated over $9B in trailing twelve-month revenue growing at 50% quarterly. Nvidia's DRIVE Hyperion platform expanded with Foxconn, VinFast, Uber, and HUMAIN partnerships. The company committed ~$150B annually in Taiwan supply chain investment, up from $10-15B five years ago, and pre-paid $119B to secure advanced packaging and HBM capacity through 2027+.

**Capital allocation** has shifted materially. The board authorized an additional $80B in share repurchases and increased the quarterly dividend 25-fold from $0.01 to $0.25. Jensen Huang committed to returning at least 50% of free cash flow to shareholders. The company returned a record $20B in Q1 alone. This signals management confidence in sustained multi-year cash generation while broadening the investor base to include income-oriented mandates.

---

## 2. Dated Recent Developments

**Computex 2026 (June 1-4):** Nvidia unveiled the RTX Spark superchip for Windows PCs (Arm-based N1X CPU co-developed with MediaTek, 1 petaflop AI performance, 128GB unified memory, fall 2026 availability), the Vera CPU for data centers, and the Vera Rubin NVL72 platform. Jensen Huang endorsed Marvell Technology as the "next trillion-dollar company" (2026-06-02, Benzinga), sending Marvell shares up 30%+. Huang also praised Nebius as a "world-class AI cloud" (2026-06-02, Motley Fool).

**Physical AI ecosystem (2026-06-01, GlobeNewswire):** Nvidia launched Cosmos 3 (open-source foundation model for physical AI), Isaac GR00T reference humanoid robot, Alpamayo 2 Super for robotaxis, DGX Station for Windows, and comprehensive open-source agent tools. Enterprise software partners including Cadence, Siemens, CrowdStrike, and Palantir are deploying Nvidia's Agent Toolkit.

**Export controls tightened (2026-05-31, Benzinga):** The U.S. Department of Commerce closed a loophole that had allowed advanced AI chips to reach Chinese firms operating outside China. License requirements now apply to entities headquartered in China regardless of location. Nvidia's China market share has effectively collapsed to zero.

**Strategic investments:** Nvidia's $5B Intel investment (December 2025 at $23.28/share) generated approximately $20B in paper profit as Intel reached $114.68/share by May 2026 (2026-06-03, Motley Fool). The company also invested $2B in Marvell and $2B in Coherent during Q1.

**Institutional positioning diverges:** Dan Loeb's Third Point reduced Nvidia by 90% in Q1 2026 (2026-06-02, Benzinga). Coatue Management also sold Nvidia (2026-05-27, Motley Fool). Conversely, Chase Coleman's Tiger Global increased its Nvidia position (2026-05-27, Motley Fool), and Glen Kacher's Light Street Capital holds 8.9% in Nvidia (2026-05-30, Motley Fool).

---

## 3. Material Risks and Offsets

**Customer concentration:** ~50% of revenue derives from five hyperscaler customers. If any major customer meaningfully shifts spend toward custom silicon (Google TPUs, Amazon Trainium, Microsoft Maia), revenue concentration risk materializes. *Offset:* All three remain among Nvidia's largest customers even while developing in-house chips; custom silicon takes 2-3 years to deploy at scale, and Nvidia refreshes architectures every 12-18 months.

**Custom ASIC competition:** Goldman Sachs projects custom ASICs will match GPU demand by 2027. Broadcom and Marvell are gaining traction designing purpose-built chips for hyperscalers. *Offset:* ASICs serve single customers for specific workloads; Nvidia's general-purpose GPUs plus CUDA ecosystem serve any AI workload, providing broader appeal and faster time-to-deployment.

**CPU workload shift:** AI inference and agentic workloads are shifting GPU:CPU ratios from 8:1 in training toward 3-4:1 in inference, potentially further for agentic applications (2026-06-03, Motley Fool citing VanEck SMH analysis). *Offset:* Nvidia is proactively entering the CPU market with Vera, targeting $20B in standalone CPU revenue this year from a $200B TAM, turning a threat into a growth vector.

**China export restrictions:** Market share in China has collapsed to zero. The Commerce Department closed remaining loopholes in May 2026. *Offset:* Non-China data center revenue grew ~120% in Q1, and sovereign AI initiatives globally (Nvidia powers 52% of tracked sovereign AI projects) provide geographic diversification.

**Valuation and market concentration:** The S&P 500's Shiller P/E reached 42, near the 1999 dot-com peak of 44. Nvidia's 7.5% index weighting creates reflexivity risk. *Offset:* Nvidia's forward P/E of ~25x is the second-lowest among Magnificent Seven peers, with 85% revenue growth and 75% gross margins supporting the multiple on a GARP basis.

**Supply constraints:** TSMC signaled capacity constraints lasting a "very long time" with potential 15% price increases for advanced nodes (2026-06-04, Benzinga). HBM memory remains sold out through 2026. *Offset:* Nvidia pre-committed $119B to secure supply through 2027+, and supply constraints actually support pricing power.

**Political/regulatory risk:** Laura Loomer raised concerns about Jensen Huang's advisory role at Tsinghua University while serving on PCAST (2026-05-28, Benzinga). Data center political backlash is emerging as a risk vector. *Offset:* These remain low-probability tail risks without concrete policy action.

---

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Positive.** Nvidia possesses a rare combination: a dominant franchise with ~86% AI GPU market share, a deep software moat (CUDA), 75% gross margins, and an asset-light fabless model generating $106B in trailing free cash flow. The business is not standing still — the Vera CPU opens a $200B TAM, physical AI is a $9B+ revenue stream growing 50% quarterly, and networking revenue is tripling as Nvidia sells architecture, not just chips. The new segment reporting (Hyperscale vs. ACIE) reveals a faster-growing enterprise/sovereign market that reduces the hyperscaler-dependency narrative. Capital allocation has pivoted decisively toward shareholder returns ($80B buyback, 25x dividend increase), and the forward P/E of ~25x is reasonable for a company guiding 95% YoY growth next quarter.

The principal structural concern is revenue concentration — 90% from Data Center, ~50% from five customers, all driven by a single technological wave. Custom silicon competition is real but moves slowly relative to Nvidia's architecture cadence. The CPU shift in inference workloads is a genuine headwind, but Nvidia's proactive Vera launch converts this from a threat into an expansion opportunity. China is effectively a zero-revenue geography, but the rest of the world is growing fast enough to more than compensate.

The franchise quality is exceptional. The competitive position is dominant but not unassailable. Structural growth vectors (CPU, physical AI, networking, sovereign AI) extend the runway meaningfully beyond the current GPU cycle. The narrative supports fundamental attractiveness.

---
